topics.name: Incident Management
topics.description: Advanced incident configuration including major incidents, escalations, parent-child relationships, and SLA management.

introduction.overview: Incident Management is the process of managing the lifecycle of all incidents to restore normal service operation as quickly as possible. This includes creation, classification, investigation, resolution, and closure of incidents while maintaining SLA compliance.
introduction.whyItMatters: Incident Management is 20% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions cover incident states, SLA behavior, major incidents, parent-child relationships, and communication with affected users.
introduction.keyConcepts: Master incident states (New, In Progress, On Hold, Resolved, Closed), SLA timelines and indicators, major incident management, parent-child incident behavior, and the difference between Work Notes (internal) and Additional Comments (customer-facing).
introduction.examTips: Remember that Incident Management focuses on quick restoration, not root cause. Know when SLAs start, pause, and end. Understand parent-child behavior especially when the parent is reopened by an end user.

topics.name: Change Management
topics.description: Standard, normal, and emergency changes with CAB approval workflows, conflict detection, and risk assessment.

introduction.overview: Change Management ensures consistent approach to risk assessment, business continuity, and change approval. It covers the complete lifecycle from creation through implementation and closure.
introduction.whyItMatters: Change Management represents 20% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Expect questions about change types, CAB/ECAB approval, conflict detection, change states, and multimodal change.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the three change types (Normal, Standard, Emergency), the difference between CAB and ECAB, scheduling and conflict detection, risk assessment methods, and change task types.
introduction.examTips: Know that Normal changes require full CAB approval, Standard changes are pre-approved, and Emergency changes need ECAB approval and should be linked to incidents. Remember the four change task types: Planning, Implementation, Testing, Review.

topics.name: Problem Management
topics.description: Root cause analysis, known error management, workarounds, and permanent solutions.

introduction.overview: Problem Management identifies and resolves the underlying cause of incidents. It involves root cause analysis, documenting workarounds, and implementing permanent solutions to prevent recurrence.
introduction.whyItMatters: Problem Management accounts for 15% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions focus on the problem lifecycle, Known Error Database (KEDB), root cause analysis, and the relationship between problems and incidents.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the three lifecycle stages (Detection/Logging, Investigation/Diagnosis, Resolution/Closure), the Known Error Database, problem tasks, and how to communicate workarounds to related incidents.
introduction.examTips: Remember that only the problem_manager role can reopen a problem. Know the two key RCA questions: 'What happened?' and 'Why did it happen?' Problems with workarounds but no permanent fix remain in the KEDB.

topics.name: Request Management
topics.description: Service requests, catalog items, record producers, and fulfillment workflows.

introduction.overview: Request Management enables the requesting and fulfilling of catalog items according to predetermined procedures. It encompasses approval workflows, task-based fulfillment, and automatic closure.
introduction.whyItMatters: Request Management is 15% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions cover the request lifecycle, catalog item types, fulfillment tasks, and the relationship between Requests, Requested Items (RITM), and Catalog Tasks (SCTASK).
introduction.keyConcepts: Master the four lifecycle stages (Submittal, Approval, Fulfillment, Closure), three catalog item types (Record Producers, Order Guides, Content Items), and the record hierarchy (REQ → RITM → SCTASK).
introduction.examTips: Know the record prefixes: REQ for requests, RITM for requested items, SCTASK for catalog tasks. Understand that Order Guides bundle multiple items. Closure flows from tasks up to request level.

topics.name: ITSM Overview
topics.description: ITSM fundamentals, ITIL alignment, and module relationships.

introduction.overview: ITSM Overview covers the foundational concepts of IT Service Management in ServiceNow, including how the core ITSM modules interact and align with ITIL best practices.
introduction.whyItMatters: ITSM Overview is 10% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions test your understanding of how Incident, Problem, Change, and Request Management interact with each other and with the CMDB.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the relationships between ITSM processes, the role of the CMDB, and how ServiceNow implements ITIL concepts.
introduction.examTips: Focus on understanding how processes hand off to each other (e.g., Incident → Problem → Change). Know the supporting applications and architecture.

topics.name: SLA Management
topics.description: SLA definitions, schedules, and breach handling.

introduction.overview: SLA Management covers the configuration and monitoring of Service Level Agreements, Operational Level Agreements (OLAs), and Underpinning Contracts (UCs).
introduction.whyItMatters: SLA Management is 10% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions focus on SLA configuration, timeline indicators, pause conditions, and breach handling.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand SLA vs OLA vs UC, SLA timeline colors (green < 50%, yellow 50-75%, orange 75-100%, red = breached, gray = paused), and how SLAs interact with incident and change states.
introduction.examTips: Know when SLA clocks start, pause, and stop. Remember the color indicators for SLA timeline status.

topics.name: Reporting & Metrics
topics.description: Reporting capabilities and key ITSM metrics.

introduction.overview: Reporting & Metrics covers ServiceNow's reporting capabilities for ITSM, including dashboards, Performance Analytics, and key metrics for service delivery.
introduction.whyItMatters: Reporting & Metrics is 10% of the CIS-ITSM exam. Questions may cover standard reports, dashboards, and understanding ITSM KPIs.
introduction.keyConcepts: Understand the reporting tools available in ServiceNow, how to create and customize dashboards, and key ITSM metrics like MTTR, first-call resolution, and SLA compliance.
introduction.examTips: Focus on understanding what metrics are important for each ITSM process and how ServiceNow provides visibility into service performance.
